takeaway: Myeloma causes lytic bone lesions and cord compression. Urine contains Bence-Jones protein, free light chains filtered by the kidney, which confirms the diagnosis.

question.text: A 65-year-old Afro-Caribbean man has back pain, tiredness and breathlessness, then cord compression. PSA is normal. Which investigation would confirm the diagnosis?
question.say: A 65-year-old Afro-Caribbean man has back pain, tiredness and breathlessness, then cord compression. P S A is normal. Which investigation would confirm the diagnosis?

lines.text: This man has back pain, tiredness and cord compression, with a normal PSA. Think myeloma.
Myeloma lytic lesions weaken the vertebrae and can compress the spinal cord.
In the marrow, crowded plasma cells make excess protein and crowd out normal blood cells.
That causes anaemia, so he is tired and breathless.
lines.say: That causes anaemia, so he is tired and breathless. (sigh)

lines.text: The kidney filters free light chains from the blood.
In about two thirds of cases they appear in the urine as Bence-Jones protein.
So a urine sample is the test that confirms the diagnosis.
